knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built from billable hours, so the running costs and income are covered by work that can be billed. Dividing by all paid hours, or using a listing average or competitor's rate, does not do this.
The lesson says a 15-minute walk does not shrink the travel, so a minimum charge covers the trip, the start of the walk and the admin. Travel and admin time does not shrink with the size of the job.

The lesson says to build the base rate from your own costs and billable hours, then compare it with local listings. A national average, a friend's rate or a listing price on one page is not a sound source.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate paid hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
